constraint_decided_it: E96 Purchase's scope note: 'a purchase agreement establishes a fixed monetary obligation at its initialization on the receiving party, to the giving party'. The case deliberately breaks that directness -- the bidder's payment obligation is discharged to the auction house, which holds it ten days and forwards only net proceeds -- so E96 is a defensible but not established refinement. A asserts it unqualified as the load-bearing class; B names it and correctly keeps it optional. Everything else is shared and clean: P22/P23 (E8 -> E39), P24 (E8 -> E18), P28/P29 (E10 -> E39), P30 (E10 -> E18), P14 (E7 -> E39, and E8/E10 are both subclasses of E7) are all applied inside their declared domains and ranges by both answers.
better_modelling: Both reach it: one instance of E8 Acquisition (optionally E96 Purchase, with P179 had sales price to an E97 Monetary Amount, which neither answer records) with P23 = the engineer, P22 = the phone bidder, P24 = the instruments; plus two instances of E10 Transfer of Custody (P28 engineer / P29 auction house, then P28 auction house / P29 courier or buyer, P30 the instruments); the auction house attaches to the Acquisition only via P14 carried out by with P14.1 in the role of. E8's and E10's scope notes both state outright that 'the CIDOC CRM therefore models legal ownership and physical custody separately', which is the clause that defeats the two-title-hop reading.
reasoning: Neither answer commits a domain, range or FOL violation, and both correctly refuse the second E8 Acquisition, since nothing in the case makes the auction house a legal owner and E8/E10 scope notes separate title from custody by design. B is better grounded on the constraint that matters: the current E10 dossier carries two published examples of exactly this configuration -- 'the transfer of custody of the work ... from Johann Matthaus von Merian to the Auction House Heldevier (Jacob) for the purpose of sale' (consignment leg) and 'the transfer of custody of the painting Mrs. Fitzherbert to the art dealer Knoedler from Parke-Bernet Galleries' (auction-house-to-buyer leg) -- both verified verbatim, while A states no source addresses the question and rests on t1376's Sotheby's/Aphrodite example, which Rob Sanderson proposed for Issue 475 and which was never adopted into the published examples (Issue 475's outcome deferred examples to Issue 516). Both answers' t1376 quotations are verbatim-accurate, and B's Issue 488 / t1345 hedge is real: that issue closed pending CRMsoc with no adopted property for 'acting at the behest of another'. B's two demerits are small -- it declines the more specific E96 (rubric 4), and it misapplies E10's P2 has type distinction, since the auction house here had actual physical possession, not merely legal responsibility for custody, and holding the buyer's money is not a custody fact at all.
